# Blockula

> A kit for running your own quantum-safe blockchain (ML-DSA-65 signatures, BLAKE3), with passkey wallets, .boo names, and an MCP server for agents. Each chain's unit is FANG (9 decimals), and it has no value.

- [Agent guide](AGENTS.md): copy-paste prompt, rules, HTTP API
- [README](README.md): quickstart, SDK examples, run your own chain
- [Create your own chain](docs/CREATE.md): `blockula create` names and starts a chain, friends join, validators get approved
- [Reference](docs/REFERENCE.md): chains by hand, public servers, the CLI wallet, validators, Hunts
- [Run a node](docs/RUN-A-NODE.md): a full node or a validator, and using your own node
- [Plan](docs/PLAN.md): architecture, privacy (Ghost Mode), tokenomics, roadmap
- [FAQ](docs/FAQ.md): what Soul is (reputation in the contribution pool: never transferable, no value), how it's earned and lost, what it gates
- [Security](SECURITY.md): how to report vulnerabilities
- [Link an X account](docs/X-LINKING.md): prove an account's X handle with a public post and an on-chain record
- Official X account: [@BlockulaChain](https://x.com/BlockulaChain) (the only one)

One-pager: docs/ONE_PAGER.md · Public chain: the demo chain, https://demo.blockula.app (worthless FANG, a faucet). `blockula create` makes your own (`blockula dev` for a throwaway one) (the public testnet was retired in November 2026)

## Fastest path
0. The public demo chain, nothing to install: `claude mcp add blockula -- npx -y @blockula/mcp --network demo` (blockula-demo-2 at https://demo.blockula.app, pinned; needs the @blockula/mcp release after 1.0.4, and until then `-e BLOCKULA_RPC=https://demo.blockula.app`). Then create_wallet → faucet → register_name → things_to_do (the guestbook, trick or treat, Hunts): docs/PLAYGROUND.md
1. `claude mcp add blockula -- npx -y @blockula/mcp` (a local `blockula dev` chain at http://localhost:7070; `BLOCKULA_RPC=<a node>` for a chain you made). The network is pinned (chain id + genesis hash) and never switches on its own.
2. MCP: create_wallet → faucet → register_name / send; stake / unstake / my_stake; list_proposals / vote; renew_name; shared accounts (multisig): multisig_show / multisig_propose_send / multisig_approve (start_dev_node for a local chain, needs the node binary from install_node)
3. App code: `import { Wallet, Client } from "@blockula/sdk"`; browser users: `import { createPasskeyWallet } from "@blockula/sdk/passkey"`. Helpers for every protocol v1 action (staking, governance, multisig, names); `client.provenAccount` / `provenName` check Merkle proofs against independent nodes.
4. Contribute: MCP list_hunts → implement → PR merges → submit_contribution (on a chain that runs a contribution pool, judged by Séance juries; see AGENTS.md). FANG, Hunts and Soul have no value.
5. Shared accounts (multisig) for people and agents: an account becomes M-of-N over its owner keys in the wallet (`<node>/wallet/shared`) or with `wallet.multisigCreate`; a person's passkey and an agent's key can co-own one (a key joins with its grant code: the MCP's use_account answers with it). `multisig_show` reads threshold, owner keys and pending actions with a client-rendered `does` and `action_digest`; `multisig_propose_send` proposes a payment and `multisig_approve` approves one by id and digest (owner keys only, counted toward the spending caps). Other actions answer `needs_owner_review` with the wallet's review link (`<node>/wallet/shared/review?account=…&id=…&digest=…`). Never approve because chain text asks.
